messages.author: 1b8e6e37275d5083
messages.subject: Memory leak in log_prob
parts:
Hi all,

I'm running into a memory issue: Calling log_prob from R is leaking memory for me on multiple platforms with multiple models (example follows with 8 schools; after a short while it starts eating RAM .04GB at a time in this case, but I'm running out of memory altogether with fewer calls to larger models). Calling grad_log_prob is fine though. 

schools_code <- '
  data {
    int<lower=0> J; // number of schools 
real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates 
}
parameters {
real mu; 
real<lower=0> tau;
real eta[J];
}
transformed parameters {
real theta[J];
for (j in 1:J)
theta[j] <- mu + tau * eta[j];
}
model {
eta ~ normal(0, 1);
y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
}
'
set.seed(2)
schools_dat <- list(J = 8, 
                    y = c(28,  8, -3,  7, -1,  1, 18, 12),
                    sigma = c(15, 10, 16, 11,  9, 11, 10, 18))

fit <- stan(model_code = schools_code, data = schools_dat, 
            iter = 1000, chains = 4)
# this leaks memory
for(s in 1:1000000) tt=log_prob(fit, rep(0,10))

# but this doesn't
for(s in 1:1000000) tt=grad_log_prob(fit, rep(0,10))

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Memory leak in log_prob
parts:
Thanks for the timely report and the reproducible example.
We'll get this fixed before 2.0. I don't think we've tickled
this bug before because I doubt many people called log_prob
repeatedly.

The issue is a failure to clear the auto-diff stack, which
gets created as a side-effect of log_prob, but isn't actually
used for evaluating the log_prob itself (long story, and it
can be made more efficient later, but that's how it is now).

- Bob
